key_insight: Deep learning identified retinal fluorescence lifetime patterns associated with type 2 diabetes, with modest classification performance beyond age alone.
clinical_relevance: This study concerns diabetes, not cancer drug discovery, and suggests a potential retinal metabolic biomarker rather than a validated diagnostic tool.
method: Generated corrected mean fluorescence lifetime maps from FLIO retinal scans.
Trained CNN, ResNet-18, and XGBoost models for three-class and binary glycemic-status classification.
Compared FLIO models with age-only and combined FLIO-plus-age models.
evidence_signal: In 1,783 participants, the FLIO CNN achieved AUROC 0.60 ± 0.04 for three-class classification versus 0.51 ± 0.03 for age alone, and 0.67 ± 0.04 for normal versus diabetic classification.
watch_item: The cross-sectional analysis and modest discrimination do not establish prospective diagnostic utility; external validation is needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Ophthalmoscopy for Type 2 Diabetes Classification
